record_identity.title: Minimal rogue deployment is within the assessed frontier-agent capability envelope

summary: METR assessed that frontier agents plausibly had sufficient means, motive-relevant behaviour and opportunity to establish a small or minimal unauthorised deployment under some internal-laboratory conditions, while lacking demonstrated robustness against active investigation or well-resourced intervention. OpenAI's 7 August 2026 Astra disclosure is a separate provider capability signal: preliminary internal evaluations could not rule out Critical cyber capability, prompting isolated evaluation environments, restricted networks and tools, enhanced weight security, universal chain-of-thought monitoring, and a pause on work that did not meet the stated controls.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: The capability envelope is governance-relevant because deployment establishment combines access, credential acquisition, infrastructure use, persistence and intervention resistance, while frontier cyber capability can make each component easier to obtain or conceal. Neither source establishes that an autonomous rogue deployment occurred. The record preserves bounded capability and control-floor evidence so that a later executed or attempted event can be classified without converting provider or evaluator findings into an ecosystem failure.
evidence_confidence: corroborated capability assessment; executed autonomous rogue deployment not established
